articles.title: DEEP SKY OBSERVING
articles.summary: This article presents a deep-sky observing list for March 2007, specifically for the period between the third quarter and new moon. Compiled by Mark Wagner, the list includes various galaxies and galaxy clusters, organized from north to south within a comfortable right ascension range for evening viewing. It serves as a sample of a more extensive list available online, providing key observational data like constellation, type, size, magnitude, right ascension, and declination for each celestial target.

articles.title: AUCTION XXVII — April 1, 2007
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its annual astronomical auction and swap meet (AUCTION XXVII) on April 1, 2007, at Houge Park in San Jose. This event serves as a fundraiser for the SJAA, offering an opportunity for astronomers of all levels to buy and sell equipment, with voluntary, tax-deductible donations requested from sales. The day will include an auction for registered items followed by a swap meet, providing a chance for the community to exchange astronomical paraphernalia.

articles.title: Messier Marathon 2007
articles.summary: The article announces the 2007 Messier Marathon, scheduled for March 17 at Henry Coe State Park, with a preparation class on March 9. It highlights the marathon's benefit for beginners to learn efficient telescope use and object finding, offering detailed charts and instructions. The event provides a unique opportunity to practice locating deep-sky objects efficiently.

articles.title: The Last 31 Days In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article summarizes significant astronomical news from January 10 to February 10, 2007. Key developments include the classification of Kepler's supernova as Type Ia, the likely permanent failure of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, and NASA's approval of the LCROSS mission to impact the Moon. Additionally, it highlights findings about night clouds on Mars, data transmission from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, the polishing phase for the James Webb Space Telescope mirrors, and the New Horizons probe's upcoming Jupiter flyby.

articles.title: A Great Big Wreck
articles.summary: The article discusses the impending collision between the Andromeda and Milky Way galaxies, projected in about 3 billion years, emphasizing that individual stars are unlikely to collide. Astronomer John Hibbard's research on the Antennae galaxies, using data from the GALEX ultraviolet telescope, reveals that while the merging galactic cores experience intense star formation from colliding gas clouds, the vast tidal tails are surprisingly quiet, suggesting they would be the safest regions during such an event.

articles.title: SJAA 2006 Financial Report
articles.summary: The SJAA 2006 Financial Report provides a comprehensive overview of the organization's income and expenditures for the year, comparing figures to 2005. It details financial activities such as membership dues, auctions, book sales, and Sky & Telescope subscriptions, with specific notes on their net profitability. The report concludes by showing an overall increase in total assets, from $19,915.83 in 2005 to $23,114.97 in 2006.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series
articles.summary: The article announces several astronomy-related events for 2007, including a lecture on March 7th by Astronaut Janice Voss about NASA's Kepler Mission to search for Earth-like planets, part of the Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series at Foothill College. It also details the annual SJAA Yosemite Public Star Party in August, inviting amateur astronomers to host public observing events. Additionally, there are mentions of a SETI Institute Open House and opportunities for Project ASTRO.

articles.title: Riverside Club's Observing Site at Landers
articles.summary: This article, part of a series, details the Riverside Astronomical Society's (RAS) five-acre observing site in Landers, near Joshua Tree National Monument. It outlines the site's amenities, including ten electrical pads for paying licensees, public power posts for all members, RV parking, tent camping, and six private roll-off observatories. The site is supported by donations, private investment, and club dues, actively used for public outreach, and offers fairly dark skies within a 90-minute drive.

articles.title: March of the Planets
articles.summary: March offers astronomers improved planetary viewing, with Saturn ideally placed and Venus shining high in the evening sky, alongside a notable Mars-Uranus conjunction. Observers can also look for the Zodiacal Light, a close approach by asteroid 2006 VV2, and potentially Comet Encke. The article also alerts readers to the early start of Daylight Savings Time and offers tips for observing and preserving night vision.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The article provides an update on the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) telescope loaner program, detailing available scopes for immediate loan to members, along with contact information for borrowing. It also lists scopes currently on loan and those with extended loan periods, indicating their status and availability for a waiting list.
